story.head: McDavid’s favorite opponent
paras: The Blues have won two in a row, while the Oilers (17-4-3) lost 3-1 to Tampa Bay on Thursday. Going in, the Oilers are first in the Pacific (second in the NHL) and the Blues seventh in the Central (18th).

The Oilers’ record (.771) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.560), largely thanks to their finishing. The Blues’ record (.545) is about what their chances are worth. If the Oilers’ record were closer to their chances, like the Blues’, these teams would be much closer in the standings, so don’t be surprised if this one is closer than the records suggest.

The Oilers lean on their stars more than any team in the league (lowest), have the league’s most dangerous power play (1st) and play slow, tight games (3rd lowest). Edmonton has scored 3.83 goals a game, the third most in the league. As for the Blues, they ice the puck less than anyone (1st) and keep things calm after the whistle (lowest). They also get some of the league’s best looks (3rd), so the Blues wait for good looks, but the Oilers settle for hopeful ones.

Connor McDavid (13 G / 42 A / 55 P in 24 GP) leads the Oilers and the whole NHL in scoring, with seven points in his last five games and a point in nine straight games against St. Louis. Leon Draisaitl (21 G / 23 A / 44 P in 24 GP) has a team-high 21 goals, tied for the most in the NHL, with eight points in his last five games. For the Blues, Robert Thomas (4 G / 16 A / 20 P in 22 GP) leads the way in scoring, with eight points in his last five games and a point in five straight games against Edmonton. Jimmy Snuggerud (12 G / 5 A / 17 P in 22 GP) has a team-high twelve goals.
Devon Levi (10-2-0 / .902 SV% in 12 GS) is in line to start for Edmonton. Jordan Binnington (2-3-1 / .841 SV% in 6 GS) has had a rough start to the season for St. Louis, but will likely start.
At home, Jim Montgomery likes to send Dvorský, Suter and Toropchenko out against opponents’ fourth lines, so watch for them against Formenton, Michaels and Joseph.
